items.text:
tonight at 19:00 i switch on 5 grok bot routines, and if they work i wake up to pull requests instead of a to-do list

here's every one, word for word, so you can steal them:

01:00 → builder
"take the top 3 cards in todo. build each one on its own branch, run the tests, open a pull request with a 3-line summary. skip anything in not in v1"

03:00 → checker
"review every open pull request against done when. test it the way a student would. mark it ready for review or file a bug card with exact steps"

04:30 → builder, round 2
"take tonight's bug cards. fix anything under 30 minutes and leave the rest with a note"

05:30 → ops
"check uptime, error logs and the bot bill. one line each, no fixes"

06:30 → report to me
"send me one message: what got built, what passed, what's blocked, what needs me. end with live payments: on or off"

the rule under all 5: nothing that needs my yes runs after midnight. merges, deploys and live keys wait until i'm awake

i'll post what they actually did tomorrow at 07:00, good or bad

the full weekend playbook is in the article below

zh-CN.title: 5 个夜间 Grok Bot 例程：醒来看到 PR 而不是待办

zh-TW.title: 5 個夜間 Grok Bot 例程：醒來看到 PR 而不是待辦
zh-TW.summary: 作者設了 5 個按時間執行的 Grok Bot 例程：1 點建置待辦前 3 張卡並開 PR，3 點審查 PR 或提 bug 卡，4:30 修 30 分鐘內的 bug，5:30 查線上狀態、錯誤日誌和費用，6:30 發一則匯報。規則是午夜後不做任何需要他確認的事，合併、部署和正式金鑰等他醒來再處理。

en.title: Five overnight Grok Bot routines: wake up to pull requests, not a to-do list
en.summary: The author scheduled five Grok Bot routines: at 1:00 build the top 3 todo cards and open PRs, at 3:00 review PRs or file bug cards, at 4:30 fix bugs under 30 minutes, at 5:30 check uptime, error logs and the bill, at 6:30 send one report. The rule: nothing that needs his yes runs after midnight; merges, deploys and live keys wait until he is awake.

ko.title: 밤새 도는 Grok Bot 루틴 5개: 아침엔 할 일 목록 대신 PR
ko.summary: 작성자는 Grok Bot 루틴 5개를 예약했다. 1시에 할 일 상위 3개 카드를 구현해 PR을 열고, 3시에 PR을 검토하거나 버그 카드를 만들고, 4시 30분에 30분 안에 고칠 수 있는 버그를 수정하고, 5시 30분에 가동 상태·오류 로그·비용을 확인하고, 6시 30분에 보고 한 통을 보낸다. 자정 이후에는 그의 승인이 필요한 일은 하지 않으며, 병합·배포·실서비스 키는 그가 깬 뒤로 미룬다.

ms.title: Lima rutin Grok Bot waktu malam: bangun dengan pull request, bukan senarai tugasan
ms.summary: Penulis menjadualkan lima rutin Grok Bot: jam 1:00 membina 3 kad teratas dan membuka PR, jam 3:00 menyemak PR atau memfailkan kad pepijat, jam 4:30 membaiki pepijat bawah 30 minit, jam 5:30 menyemak uptime, log ralat dan bil, jam 6:30 menghantar satu laporan. Peraturannya: tiada apa yang memerlukan persetujuannya berjalan selepas tengah malam; merge, deploy dan kunci live menunggu dia bangun.

vi.title: 5 routine Grok Bot chạy qua đêm: sáng dậy là có pull request thay vì danh sách việc
vi.summary: Tác giả lên lịch 5 routine Grok Bot: 1 giờ làm 3 thẻ đầu trong todo và mở PR, 3 giờ review PR hoặc tạo thẻ lỗi, 4 giờ 30 sửa lỗi dưới 30 phút, 5 giờ 30 kiểm tra uptime, log lỗi và hóa đơn, 6 giờ 30 gửi một báo cáo. Quy tắc: sau nửa đêm không chạy việc gì cần anh đồng ý; merge, deploy và khóa live chờ anh thức dậy.

fr.title: Cinq routines Grok Bot de nuit : se réveiller avec des pull requests, pas une liste de tâches
fr.summary: L'auteur a programmé cinq routines Grok Bot : à 1 h, réaliser les 3 premières cartes et ouvrir des PR ; à 3 h, relire les PR ou créer des cartes de bug ; à 4 h 30, corriger les bugs de moins de 30 minutes ; à 5 h 30, vérifier disponibilité, logs d'erreurs et facture ; à 6 h 30, envoyer un rapport. Règle : rien qui nécessite son accord ne tourne après minuit ; merges, déploiements et clés de production attendent son réveil.

es.title: Cinco rutinas nocturnas de Grok Bot: despertar con pull requests, no con pendientes
es.summary: El autor programó cinco rutinas de Grok Bot: a la 1:00 construir las 3 primeras tarjetas y abrir PR, a las 3:00 revisar PR o abrir tarjetas de bug, a las 4:30 corregir bugs de menos de 30 minutos, a las 5:30 revisar disponibilidad, logs de errores y factura, y a las 6:30 enviar un informe. Regla: nada que requiera su aprobación corre después de medianoche; merges, despliegues y claves en vivo esperan a que despierte.

de.title: Fünf nächtliche Grok-Bot-Routinen: morgens Pull Requests statt To-do-Liste
de.summary: Der Autor plante fünf Grok-Bot-Routinen: um 1:00 die obersten 3 Karten bauen und PRs öffnen, um 3:00 PRs prüfen oder Bug-Karten anlegen, um 4:30 Bugs unter 30 Minuten beheben, um 5:30 Uptime, Fehlerlogs und Kosten prüfen, um 6:30 einen Bericht senden. Regel: Nach Mitternacht läuft nichts, was seine Zustimmung braucht; Merges, Deploys und Live-Schlüssel warten, bis er wach ist.

YOUR FIRST GROK BOT SHOULD BE BORING ENOUGH TO TRUST.

most people see “AI teammate” and immediately design an org chart: a stack of roles, every available tool, and a vague mission to “run the business.”

it looks ambitious. it is also impossible to debug when the output goes wrong.

the smarter first move is narrower. give one Grok Bot one workflow with a visible finish line. every morning, it reviews unread customer emails, groups them by urgency, researches the missing context, and prepares replies for approval.

then judge the handoff, not the performance.

did it use the right sources? 
did it preserve context?
did it return at the right decision point? 
did it remove more work than it created?

if it fails, the scope is small enough to correct once and test again. if it works, you now have a repeatable unit that can expand without pretending to be an entire company.

the first useful Grok Bot will not feel like a new department.

it will feel like one task you stopped carrying.

zh-CN.summary: 作者建议别一上来就搭一整套角色组织，而是给一个 Grok Bot 一条有明确终点的流程：每天早上看未读客户邮件、按紧急度分组、补齐缺失背景、准备回复等你批准。然后评估交接：来源对不对、上下文是否保留、是否在该决策时交回、省的活是否多于添的活。

zh-TW.title: 第一個 Grok Bot 要無聊到值得信任
zh-TW.summary: 作者建議別一開始就搭一整套角色組織，而是給一個 Grok Bot 一條有明確終點的流程：每天早上看未讀客戶郵件、按緊急程度分組、補齊缺少的背景、準備回覆等你核准。然後評估交接：來源對不對、脈絡是否保留、是否在該決策時交回、省下的工作是否多於增加的。

en.summary: Instead of designing an org chart of roles, the author suggests giving one Grok Bot one workflow with a visible finish line: every morning it reviews unread customer emails, groups them by urgency, researches missing context and prepares replies for approval. Then judge the handoff: right sources, preserved context, returning at the decision point, and removing more work than it creates.

Kemudian nilai serahannya: sumber betul, konteks terpelihara, kembali pada titik keputusan, dan mengurangkan lebih banyak kerja daripada yang ditambah.

Puis juger la passation : bonnes sources, contexte préservé, retour au bon moment de décision, et plus de travail retiré qu'ajouté.

Dann die Übergabe bewerten: richtige Quellen, erhaltener Kontext, Rückmeldung am Entscheidungspunkt und mehr Arbeit abgenommen als erzeugt.

YOU ARE PAYING SENIOR RATES TO RENAME FILES

the setup everyone is reposting is OpenAI Dots plus Claude Code as one dev team. the part actually worth stealing is smaller than that: which model gets the task first.

Sonnet 5.5 reads at $2 per million and writes at $10. Opus 5.5 is double on both.

~/project-x $ claude -p "Fix issue #381. Run the tests. Open a pull request." --model claude-sonnet-5-5

here's the split:

▸ Sonnet takes the first pass on everything, 2 tries maximum
▸ Opus gets it only when Sonnet is stuck, 1 try, and it plans instead of typing
▸ tests decide, not the model. 318 of 318 or the task is not done
▸ you approve the pull request, and nothing merges itself

on 1,000 tasks that is roughly $480 instead of $800 for the same work, because the expensive brain only wakes up for the 20% that earns it.

the part that makes this safe: the Dot never merges. it opens the issue, reads the result and writes you a summary. the branch, the commits and the test output all live in GitHub, so neither model has to remember anything.

by 08:00 there is a PR waiting with no database changes and your approval missing, not a commit you have to undo.

the benchmarks are closer than that price gap suggests. Sonnet beats Opus on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 70.6 to 66.4. Opus pulls ahead on the long messy ones, FrontierCode 54.4 to 46.2. that spread is the entire reason a router exists.

one honest warning: there is no connect button. OpenAI and Anthropic ship nothing that joins these two. you build the GitHub bridge yourself, and if your tests are weak you have only automated a bad merge faster.

8 hours of nothing becomes 9 tasks routed, fixed and green before you open the laptop.

save it, this is the cheapest senior engineer you will ever avoid hiring.

How to choose between Muse and Grok Bot

The least useful agent comparison copies two feature lists and declares a winner. In practice, a disconnected tool, an unusable deliverable, or an unexpected action can matter more than the length of either list.

My recommendation is a testing order: start with Meta Muse for personal administration and goals; evaluate Grok Bot first for named responsibilities, recurring deliverables, and work across tools. Their capabilities overlap. This is a reading of official materials checked on October 28, 2026, not a head-to-head performance result.

Start with how the work is organized

Meta introduced Muse on September 8 and announced its Japan launch on October 23. These are existing developments, not news breaking today. Its positioning centers on a person’s goals, schedule, and everyday administration. [1] [2]

Grok Bot emphasizes named Bots with defined jobs and durable working context. Its skills describe how work is done; routines determine when it runs. [3] [4] That makes it worth testing first when you want an ongoing industry researcher and a separate editorial responsibility.

This is a preference, not a capability wall. Muse’s design article also describes a terminal, document and webpage creation, and continuing background work. [5] It is not limited to personal errands. Compare how much explanation and correction each product needs for your recurring tasks.

Check eligibility before designing the workflow. A regional Muse announcement does not establish worldwide access. Grok Bot’s current documentation lists compatible Cursor and SuperGrok subscriptions, among others; an X badge alone is not sufficient evidence of access. [2] [3] Verify the actual plan, limits, and connections available to your account.

The overlooked distinction is the permission boundary

Grok Bot’s detailed documentation says that Bots on the same account share a cloud computer, including files, browser sessions, and command-line credentials. Separate screens are not separate security boundaries. [6] Naming three Bots Researcher, Finance Assistant, and Personal Assistant does not automatically isolate their data.

Sharing makes handoffs easier: another Bot can continue saved work. It also changes what belongs in that environment. If clients or data classifications require strict separation, role descriptions are insufficient. Verify the product’s account or organizational isolation options; do not connect the data if those controls fail your requirements.

Muse’s security article describes separating the agent runtime from sensitive services, with an independent Sentinel controlling connector actions and network egress. [7] That is a vendor-disclosed architecture, not my security audit or proof of zero risk. Neither product’s documentation establishes that the other is necessarily unsafe.

Test a complete workflow

Consider a weekly technology brief. My proposed workflow is to collect specified sources with event dates, shortlist three candidates, prepare bilingual copy and illustrations, verify facts and calculations, and check that delivered files open. Stop at a reviewable draft. Missing sources should produce a gap report, not recycled figures presented as current.

In Grok Bot, start with one Bot completing the whole task before splitting research and editing. Its documentation recommends validating a one-time task before saving a skill and scheduling a routine. [4] Adding Bots too early may add handoff and debugging costs. Apply identical acceptance criteria to Muse; a terminal and file-generation capability do not establish delivery quality.

Define authorization separately for sending, purchasing, and publishing. Grok Bot documents approvals and Auto Review rules: Ask first takes precedence when it also matches an Allow automatically rule. Muse describes confirmation for consequential actions too. [1] [8] The account, recipient, and exact version must be identifiable. Website operation does not establish permission for every platform automation. Validate drafting and publishing separately.

The revealing cases are an expired login, an inaccessible source, or a damaged attachment. Does it stop and explain, or claim completion? Can it resume from a checkpoint without repeating an external action? Include those cases rather than judging only a smooth demonstration.

Price your review time as well as the subscription

Take a hypothetical example unrelated to either product’s actual plans. Suppose one option costs an extra $20 per month but saves two human minutes per accepted task. At $30 per hour, that releases $1 of time value per task. Twenty tasks cover the extra fee; 10 release $10 and 50 release $50.

The break-even assumes no additional setup or recovery cost. Extra costs raise the required volume. Released time is not necessarily cash savings: it matters only if time is actually freed and the opportunity-cost assumption is meaningful. Free entry does not mean zero total cost, and a higher fee does not establish better capability.

I would test the same 10 tasks on both products, repeating each batch twice: five sourced research summaries, three content deliverables, and two spreadsheet outputs. Keep sources, acceptance criteria, and budgets equal. Add expired-login and missing-source tests. If a product cannot deliver an item, record that instead of quietly substituting an easier task.

Track acceptable deliverables, human review minutes per task, serious errors, recovery outcomes, and total costs. Include failed attempts and rework. Ten tasks are a starting point, not proof of general reliability. The goal is to choose for your work, not crown a universal winner.

My decision

For personal preferences and life administration, I would start with Muse. For recurring research, file delivery, and explicit responsibilities, I would evaluate Grok Bot first. That preference follows their product organization, not a ranking of model intelligence.

If the necessary connection, regional access, subscription, or data separation is missing, postpone the migration. Watch recovery, visible permissions, accepted-delivery rate, and review effort—not only new model names. Keep the product that reduces repeated explanation and rework on your tasks.

Meta Museの興味深い利用例（Xユーザー・実例中心） $META

お金・請求まわり
•電話・ネット回線の値引き交渉（実際に電話もかける）：AT&Tを$80→$40、Spectrumを$75→$40、Verizonを$516→$386など。Peter Yang氏は年$800超節約したと報告。
•自動車保険の見直し：$3,500/年節約（同じ補償）、別事例では$500→$335/月に当日切り替え。
•フライト遅延補償：7時間遅延でDeltaから$250クレジットを約5分で取得＋再予約。
•運賃下落監視：予約済みフライトを監視して値下がり時にクレジット取得（$1,000超の例あり）。
•未請求金の発見：州の未請求財産から$1,500超を5分程度で見つけ、申請書類まで作成。
•サブスク監査：メールや明細を見て使っていないものを解約し、月$100超・年$1,200相当の節約例。

旅行・予約
•日本旅行のレストラン予約を全部Museに任せ、箱根のホテルに日本語で交渉して非公開ディナーを確保した例。
•フライト・ホテル・移動・レストランを一気に組む。カレンダー連携で空き時間を見て予約。

生活・その他
•Facebook Marketplaceで出品・交渉・購入者対応。
•「タコスの火曜日」みたいな曖昧な指示からInstacartでカート作成〜決済まで。
•古いメール数万通の整理、返品手続き、HVACメンテ予約など、面倒な事務作業をまとめて処理。
•求人応募を数十件自動化して面接まで進めた例。
•イベント準備（ボランティア登録・メール対応・スケジュール作成）を任せて、当日は行くだけ。

傾向 特に「請求交渉・保険見直し・返金・未請求金」が突出して効果を出しており、Xでも「Museが一番使ってるAIになった」「Claude解約した」といった声が見られます。買い物・予約系も多いですが、Amazonはブロックするなどサイトによる制限もあります。

MuseはAmazonにブロックされて買い物出来ないの？ $META $AMZN

はい、Amazonでは買い物できません。
AmazonはMeta Museのローンチ直後（2026年9月中旬頃）から、Museによるhttps://t.co/j1CQEwpazcへのアクセスをブロックしています。
状況
•MuseでAmazonを開こうとすると、「Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use」というポップアップが出て進めない。
•Amazon側は「事前に許可を求めていない」「エージェントが自分を名乗らない」「ログイン情報を扱うリスクがある」として、MetaにAmazonをMuseの対象から外すよう要請したが、応じなかったためブロックした、と説明しています。
背景 Amazonは自社の「Buy for Me」などのエージェントを推進しつつ、他社のエージェント（以前はPerplexityなども）が自サイトで買い物するのを積極的に防いでいます。Muse以外にも、一部の小売業者がエージェントによる購入を拒否する動きが出ています。
代わりにできること
•Walmart、Best Buy、Sephora、Wayfair、Shopify系店舗など、Museと連携している店舗や、ブロックされていないサイトでは買い物可能。
•Amazon以外の一般的なサイトなら、ブラウザ経由で操作できるケースが多いです。
現状、Amazonでの買い物は事実上使えない状態です。

In 10 weeks, 4 AI labs shipped personal agents that never log off.
Most researchers will hand them the wrong jobs.

This month I finished my April travel reimbursements.
6 months late.

Federally funded PIs spend an estimated 44% of research time on admin.
ChatGPT cleared my pile in one sitting. 
Then it hit me. An always-on agent would never let the pile form.

What I'd tell any researcher setting one up:

1️⃣ Decide what it handles without telling you
↳ Do: easy to undo. Filing receipts.
↳ Digest: weekly. New papers.
↳ Ping: urgent and rare. A retraction of a paper you cite.
↳ Ask: anything sent in your name.

2️⃣ Every extra alert makes you likelier to miss the urgent one
↳ Clinicians override 49% to 96% of drug safety alerts.
↳ Keep the Ping lane tiny.

3️⃣ Literature updates don't need an always-on agent
↳ A scheduled weekly search in Claude or ChatGPT is enough.
↳ Keep your PubMed alert as a scheduled task (personal AI agents is overkill).

4️⃣ What it can see matters more than how smart it is
↳ Mine reads my personal Gmail, not my institutional inbox. Work email and patient data wait for institutional approval.
↳ Meta just paused Muse's chat sharing after about 6,800 shared links surfaced in public DNS records.

5️⃣ Start with a job where a mistake is easy to undo
↳ Receipts, filed by meeting as they arrive. You still press submit.

One catch: Dots aren't on ChatGPT Plus, and Claude Duet is a US waitlist. 

💬 Which admin job would you hand off first?

More on AI for academic research in my free newsletter (16,000+ researchers): https://t.co/XTq6dj6SoB

fr.title: Cinq conseils aux chercheurs qui configurent un agent toujours actif
fr.summary: Conseils d'un chercheur : classer les tâches en Faire (facile à annuler, comme ranger des reçus), Résumé hebdomadaire, Alerte urgente et rare, et Demander pour tout ce qui part en votre nom ; garder les alertes au minimum, car trop d'alertes masquent l'urgent ; une recherche hebdomadaire planifiée suffit pour la veille bibliographique ; ce que l'agent voit compte plus que son intelligence, donc le sien lit son Gmail perso, pas sa boîte institutionnelle ; et commencer par des tâches faciles à annuler.

es.title: Cinco consejos para investigadores que configuran un agente siempre activo
es.summary: Consejos de un investigador: dividir las tareas en Hacer (fácil de deshacer, como archivar recibos), Resumen semanal, Aviso urgente y poco frecuente, y Preguntar para todo lo que se envía en tu nombre; mantener mínimo el canal de avisos porque el exceso oculta lo urgente; una búsqueda semanal programada basta para la literatura; importa más lo que puede ver que lo listo que es, así que el suyo lee su Gmail personal, no el correo institucional; y empezar por tareas fáciles de deshacer.

de.title: Fünf Tipps für Forschende, die einen dauerhaft aktiven Agenten einrichten
de.summary: Rat eines Forschers: Aufgaben in Erledigen (leicht rückgängig zu machen, etwa Belege ablegen), wöchentlichen Digest, seltenen dringenden Ping und Nachfragen bei allem, was in deinem Namen rausgeht, aufteilen; den Ping-Kanal klein halten, weil zu viele Alarme das Dringende verdecken; für Literatur genügt eine geplante Wochensuche; wichtiger als Intelligenz ist, was er sehen darf, daher liest seiner das private Gmail, nicht das Dienstpostfach; und mit leicht umkehrbaren Aufgaben beginnen.

items.text:
I won't pick a daily driver for my autonomous agent before I've tried @Claude Duet.

So far, I like @OpenAI Dot. It looks very promising, but it doesn't evolve much, at least from what I see, and it can't safely drive more than 2 or 3 sessions in parallel.

@Muse is surprisingly good and polished, maybe the most proactive of them all. But it doesn't feel built for work, and I don't need an agent to find me a hotel. I don't even let my wife do that.

Then there's Grok @bot. I have one for X, but I haven't gone deep with it. It was really dumb a few times at the beginning, and I lost the little trust I'd given it. The hype is real, though, and half of tech bro Twitter is rooting for it, including people I respect like @theo. It has to be good. I want to believe.

I still have a Hermes agent. I love it for research and for discussing ideas, not for doing the actual work. And I have an OpenClaw agent enjoying an early retirement. You can call it nostalgia. 6 months feels like a century in AI land.

Now, I have big hopes for Duet because, on paper, it's built for people like me: small business owners juggling way too many balls. Like OpenAI Dot, it would have access to my repos, hundreds of sessions, skills, plugins and historical data. An agent needs context, and seriously good access to Codex and Claude.

To make up my mind while waiting for Duet, I'm closely following a few people who build these projects or have real influence on them. An agent, alone or running a swarm, takes time to set up properly in your ecosystem before it gives its best, and I don't have the bandwidth to do that 2 or 3 times.

We are back to the Android vs iOS thing, where you definitely need to pick a side if you want the best of it.

If you are in a similar situation and don't follow them yet, start here: @ahuja_karan, @gabemulley, @embirico, @TheRohanVarma, @christinesed, @dps, @poteto (of course!) and @romanugarte.
